Parked for 49 Years: 1971 Pontiac Needs Restoration, Mixed News Under the Hood
28 photos
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us
Sitting since 1977. This is the first thing you must know about this Trans Am, with the car begging for a complete restoration after spending all these decades away from the road.
Before it can even start dreaming about this long overdue return to the road, the Pontiac has another big mission to accomplish. It must find a home, as the owner posted it on eBay, along with a few specifics about its past.
Most of the original parts are on the car, according to the owner, and that’s the good news. The bad news is that the Trans Am hides a non-original block under the hood, so if you’re here specifically because you want an all-original Pontiac , you’ll just have to look somewhere else.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The Trans Am was still in its early days in 1971. Having been launched in 1969, the Trans Am accounted for only 2,116 orders two years later, therefore being the rarest configuration in 1971.
The base Firebird dominated the lineup with 23,021 cars sold to American buyers, followed by the Esprit that accounted for 20,185 units. The Formula was more than three times as popular as the Trans Am, representing 7,802 cars.
1971 was a year when the muscle under the hood still played an important role for American drivers, and despite the push for smaller displacement and more efficient engines, Pontiac didn’t want to give up on big engines.
It reduced the compression but upgraded the 400ci unit on the Trans Am to 455 cubic inches. Known as 455-HO, this engine was the only choice on the Trans Am, though it was offered with either a manual or an automatic transmission. Most people picked the automatic, while the manual made its way to 885 cars.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The Trans Am was only offered in two visual configurations. You could get the car either in Cameo White with blue stripes or in Lucerne Blue with white stripes.
This 1971 Trans Am sports the white paint with blue stripes, though it’s unclear if this is the factory spray. I would call the seller and ask for more specifics on this front, but as I said every time I come across a mysterious car, nothing beats a live inspection. Just go there in person to check everything live, as there’s always a good chance that you’ll discover more than what you find online.
Otherwise, this Trans Am hasn’t moved in so many decades, and we all know what this means from a mechanical perspective. While the block isn’t original, it does sport the 1971 casting, so it’s a correct unit that somehow ended up in this Trans Am.
It’s unclear what happened with the original engine, but considering the many years of sitting, I wouldn’t be surprised to discover that the factory unit was seized and the owner found a replacement once they decided to bring the car back to the road.
This Trans Am needs a complete restoration, and the seller also includes a new interior. There are many other parts that you’ll get with this Pontiac, so in many ways, the restoration process has already been jump-started to pave the way for a faster return to the road.
Photo: eBay seller emarkou-us The car has over 83,000 miles on it, according to the seller, and considering it’s been sitting for so many years, the original owner enjoyed driving it quite a lot. The Trans Am was parked in 1977, so all these miles were added in only 6 years.
There’s one very important thing you must remember about this Trans Am. It sells without a transmission, so depending on your choice, you can go either for a manual or pick an automatic. A manual would be the right way to enjoy driving this car, but automatics are easier to find, though this also depends on where you live and whether you can find a gearbox fast.
Otherwise, this Trans Am looks doable, and if you don’t mind the non-original setup, it could be a fantastic project that could end up becoming quite a head-turner.
The selling price could be an issue, though. Sure, it’s a 1971 model, and these cars are pretty rare, considering only a few have been made, in the first place. But without the original engine under the hood, it might be hard to convince a restoration guy to pay $46,500 for this car.
The owner also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so they might be interested in discussing the asking price if you’re committed to a purchase. 30 people added this Trans Am to their watchlists, and considering the listing expires in 28 days, the number could increase significantly in the coming weeks.
Meanwhile, the car is parked in Lemont, Illinois, and given that the engine no longer starts or runs, you will need transportation to take it home. Just make sure it’s large enough to get all the extra parts.
Via // eBay
